drivingQuestion: From where is it derived that a leper's sin and guilt offerings require libations?
outcomeNote: source supplied by a baraita, whose exposition likely continues in the next unit

segments.he: אֶלָּא שֶׁחַטָּאתוֹ שֶׁל מְצוֹרָע וַאֲשָׁמוֹ טָעוּן נְסָכִים, מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״וּשְׁלֹשָׁה עֶשְׂרוֹנִים סֹלֶת מִנְחָה״ – בְּמִנְחָה הַבָּאָה עִם הַזֶּבַח הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that in general sin offerings and guilt offerings do not require libations. «But» the exception is «that the sin offering of a leper and his guilt offering require libations.» The Gemara asks: «From where are these matters» derived? They are derived from a verse, «as the Sages taught» in a baraita concerning the following verse, which details the offerings a leper is required to bring as part of his purification process: “And on the eighth day he shall take two unblemished male lambs, and one unblemished female lamb in its year, «and three-tenths of fine flour for a meal offering,» mixed with oil, and one log of oil” (Leviticus 14:10). The baraita explains: It is «with regard to a meal offering that comes with» an animal «offering» that «the verse speaks,» and so it is stating that each of the three offerings mentioned requires libations.
